scales.title: C major
scales.tip: Right hand. After finger 3, tuck the thumb under to F.

scales.title: G major
scales.tip: Same fingering. F♯ is the only black key.

scales.title: A harmonic minor
scales.tip: Raise G to G♯: the leading tone pulls home to A.

scales.title: D major
scales.tip: Two black keys, F♯ and C♯. LH 5-4-3-2-1-3-2-1.

songs.title: House of the Rising Sun
songs.uses: chords Am C D F E

remember: Find C: it sits just left of every pair of black keys.
Your thumbs are finger 1. Your pinkies are finger 5.
Sit tall. Round your fingers like you are holding a ball.
child.care: Clean hands, no drinks on the piano, and close the lid when you finish.

beginner.build: Play fingers 1-2-3-4-5 with each hand. Make every note the same loudness.
beginner.play: Play a five-note song like “Hot Cross Buns” with a steady beat.
beginner.check: You can find every C and play a little song without stopping.

intermediate.build: Learn the C, G and F scales. Tuck your thumb under to keep going.
intermediate.play: Play hands together, slowly. Try loud (forte) and soft (piano).
intermediate.check: You can play a short piece hands together and keep the beat.

advanced.build: Play every scale and chord. Use the right pedal to join sounds together.
advanced.play: Make the tune sing louder than the notes underneath it.
advanced.check: You can play a piece for people from memory and make it tell a story.

remember: C is just left of every pair of black keys; middle C is the one nearest the center.
Finger numbers run thumb 1 to pinky 5, the same on both hands.
Curved fingers and loose wrists, and a steady beat before speed.
teen.care: Clean, dry hands. Keep things off the lid, dust the keys with a dry cloth, and tune it once or twice a year.

beginner.build: Five-finger patterns in C and G, one hand at a time, slow and even (60 BPM).
beginner.play: Melodies with simple left-hand notes, counting 1-2-3-4 out loud.
beginner.check: You can name any white key, read a simple melody and keep a steady count.

intermediate.build: Two-octave major scales, triads and their inversions, hands together with a metronome.
intermediate.play: Hands-together pieces with dynamics (p, mf, f), legato and staccato, and the damper pedal.
intermediate.check: You can learn a one-page piece in a week with the right notes, rhythm and dynamics.

advanced.build: All major and minor scales and arpeggios; I–IV–V–I in every key.
advanced.play: Bring the melody out over the accompaniment, shape each phrase, and pedal by ear.
advanced.check: You can perform a memorized piece for an audience, recover from slips and explain your choices.

remember: Navigate by the black keys: C sits left of the pair, F left of the trio; middle C is near the center.
Finger numbers (1 = thumb, 5 = little finger) are printed above notes; follow them from day one.
Tone comes from a free arm and curved fingers; slow, even practice beats fast, uneven practice.
adult.care: Keep room humidity steady (about 40–50%) and liquids off the case; tune every 6–12 months. Digital pianos need only dusting.

beginner.build: Five-finger positions in C and G; evenness at a slow metronome setting before any speed.
beginner.play: Simple melodies over single left-hand notes or fifths, counting aloud throughout.
beginner.check: You can read and play a hands-separate piece at a steady pulse without stopping to fix mistakes.

intermediate.build: Two-octave major and harmonic minor scales; triads and inversions; hands together at a set tempo.
intermediate.play: Independent articulation in each hand; legato pedaling (lift as the new chord sounds, press again just after).
intermediate.check: You can prepare a short piece in two weeks with accurate rhythm, consistent fingering and clear dynamics.

advanced.build: All major and minor scales and arpeggios at speed; diatonic progressions and transposition into any key.
advanced.play: Voicing, rubato and pedaling by ear across styles (Baroque, Classical, Romantic, jazz).
advanced.check: You can perform a memorized program, recover from slips without stopping and justify your interpretive choices.

scales.title: E minor pentatonic (open strings)
scales.tip: Start on the thickest string: open, then a fret. Every E is a home note.

listen.name: Elizabeth Cotten
listen.what: taught herself, playing a guitar upside down

listen.name: Sister Rosetta Tharpe
listen.what: the godmother of rock and roll

scales.title: E minor pentatonic (open strings)
scales.tip: Start on the thickest string: open, then a fret. Every E is a home note.

scales.title: A minor pentatonic (5th position)
scales.tip: The box most rock and blues solos start from. Index finger on fret 5.

songs.title: Wish You Were Here
songs.uses: chords G C D Am Em

scales.title: A minor pentatonic (5th position)
scales.tip: The box most rock and blues solos start from. Index finger on fret 5.

scales.title: G major (open position)
scales.tip: One finger per fret: fret 1 = finger 1 … fret 4 = finger 4.

songs.title: Hotel California
songs.uses: chords Bm F♯ A E G D Em

remember: Strings from fat to thin: E A D G B E (“Every Amazing Dog Gets Big Ears”).
Press just behind the metal fret with the tip of your finger.
Your pointer finger is 1. Your pinky is 4.
child.care: Keep it in its case or on a stand. Wipe the strings after you play.

beginner.build: Play one string at a time until each note rings clear, with no buzz.
beginner.play: Play an easy tune on one or two strings with a steady beat.
beginner.check: You can tune with a tuner app and play notes that ring clearly.

intermediate.build: Learn E minor, G, C and D. Practice switching between two of them.
intermediate.play: Strum down, down-up, up-down-up while you change chords on time.
intermediate.check: You can strum a whole song with four chords and never stop the beat.

advanced.build: Play barre chords and scales up and down the whole neck.
advanced.play: Play a melody and chords together, or a solo with bends and slides.
advanced.check: You can play a song for people and keep going after a mistake.

remember: Open strings, low to high: E A D G B E. String 6 is the thickest.
Fret just behind the fret wire on your fingertip; fingers 1–4 run index to pinky.
Tune before every session. Clean notes beat fast notes.
teen.care: Store it in a case away from heaters, wipe the strings after playing, and change strings when they sound dull.

beginner.build: Clean single notes on every string; alternate down and up picking at 60 BPM.
beginner.play: Single-note riffs and melodies from tab, counting 1-2-3-4 out loud.
beginner.check: You can tune, read tab and play a riff where every note rings without buzzing.

intermediate.build: Open chords (G C D E A Em Am Dm), one-minute change drills, and the minor pentatonic scale.
intermediate.play: Common progressions like I–V–vi–IV with strumming patterns, palm muting and dynamics.
intermediate.check: You can play a full song with clean changes on the beat, along with a recording or your own singing.

advanced.build: Barre chords, CAGED shapes, pentatonic and major scales across the neck; bends, slides and hammer-ons.
advanced.play: Improvise over a 12-bar blues, arrange a melody with chords, and play in a band.
advanced.check: You can perform a set, improvise a solo that fits the chords and play by ear in any key.

remember: Standard tuning, string 6 to 1: E2 A2 D3 G3 B3 E4. Guitar sounds an octave lower than written.
Fret close to the fret wire on the fingertip with the least pressure that gives a clear note.
Short daily practice builds calluses and coordination more safely than long, occasional sessions.
adult.care: Keep humidity steady (about 45–55%), wipe strings after use, and restring when the tone dulls or tuning starts to drift.

beginner.build: Clean single notes across all strings; alternate picking with a metronome; finger-independence drills.
beginner.play: Simple riffs and melodies in first position, then your first two-chord songs.
beginner.check: You can tune on your own and play a short melody accurately at a steady tempo.

intermediate.build: All open chords with timed changes; major and minor pentatonic in one position; fingerpicking with p-i-m-a.
intermediate.play: Diatonic progressions with varied strumming or fingerstyle; dynamics and palm muting.
intermediate.check: You can accompany a song from a chord chart at tempo, with every change landing on the beat.

advanced.build: Barre and extended chords, the CAGED system, major, minor and modal scales across the neck, legato and in-tune bends.
advanced.play: Improvising over chord changes, chord-melody arranging, playing by ear and ensemble interplay.
advanced.check: You can perform with confidence, improvise melodically over changes and transpose a song on demand.

scales.title: D major on the D and A strings
scales.tip: Fingers 2 and 3 sit close together.

listen.name: Itzhak Perlman
listen.what: one of the world’s great violinists

scales.title: D major
scales.tip: High 2: fingers 2 and 3 touch.

scales.title: A major
scales.tip: Same pattern, one string higher.

scales.title: G major, two octaves
scales.tip: High 2 on G and D strings, low 2 on A and E.

scales.title: D major
scales.tip: Check each 3rd finger against the next open string.

remember: Strings from low to high: G D A E (“Good Dogs Always Eat”).
Bow straight across the strings, halfway between the bridge and the fingerboard.
Make a bunny hand on the bow: thumb bent, fingers soft.
child.care: Loosen the bow hair after you play. Wipe off the rosin dust. Never leave it on a chair.

beginner.build: Long, straight bows on open strings. Listen for smooth, not scratchy.
beginner.play: Play “Twinkle” rhythms on open strings, then a little tune.
beginner.check: You can hold the violin and bow by yourself and play open strings smoothly.

intermediate.build: Practice the D major and A major scales. Check each note with a tuner.
intermediate.play: Play songs with smooth joined notes (slurs) and short bouncy notes.
intermediate.check: You can play a whole song in tune with a nice sound.

advanced.build: Learn shifting and vibrato (a gentle wobble that makes a note sing).
advanced.play: Play with other people, like in an orchestra, and follow the conductor.
advanced.check: You can play a piece for people with a beautiful sound, in tune, start to finish.

remember: Open strings, low to high: G D A E. Finger 0 is open; 1–4 run index to pinky.
A straight bow at the contact point, between bridge and fingerboard; let arm weight make the sound.
Relaxed left thumb and jaw. Tension is the enemy of playing in tune.
teen.care: Loosen the bow hair after playing, rosin only every few sessions, wipe the strings and top, and check that the bridge stands straight.

beginner.build: Open-string bowing with whole bows, then half bows; finger pattern 0-1-2-3 checked with a tuner.
beginner.play: Folk tunes in D and A major using one finger pattern.
beginner.check: You can tune with the fine tuners, play one-octave D and A major scales and draw a clear, straight bow.

intermediate.build: Two-octave scales; détaché, slurs and staccato; bow distribution (which part of the bow, and how much).
intermediate.play: Orchestra or duet parts, shaping phrases with bow speed and weight.
intermediate.check: You can play in tune with others, follow the bowings and control loud and soft.

advanced.build: Three-octave scales, shifting, vibrato, spiccato and double stops.
advanced.play: Solo pieces with your own expressive choices; listening and leading in chamber music.
advanced.check: You can perform a solo with accurate intonation, vibrato and varied tone color.

remember: Tuned in perfect fifths: G3 D4 A4 E5. Tune A first (A440), then the others to it.
Tone depends on bow speed, weight and contact point; keep the bow parallel to the bridge.
Balance, not grip: jaw and collarbone support the instrument so the left hand stays free.
adult.care: Loosen the hair after every session, wipe rosin off strings and varnish, case it at steady humidity, and let a luthier fix a leaning bridge.

beginner.build: Straight bowing on open strings with even tone; the first finger pattern (high 2) checked with a tuner or drone.
beginner.play: Simple folk tunes and duets in D, A and G major.
beginner.check: You can tune with the fine tuners and play one-octave scales in tune with a steady, straight bow.

intermediate.build: Two-octave scales and arpeggios; détaché, legato, staccato and martelé; control of bow distribution and speed.
intermediate.play: Ensemble playing; phrase shaping through bow speed, weight and contact point.
intermediate.check: You can play in tune in an ensemble, follow conductor and bowings, and shape dynamics on purpose.

advanced.build: Three-octave scales, double stops, spiccato and sautillé, vibrato control, intonation against drones.
advanced.play: Solo and chamber repertoire across styles with informed interpretation.
advanced.check: You can perform with secure intonation, a range of tone colors and musical choices you can explain.

scales.title: Your first notes
scales.tip: Black circle = press that key. Left hand on top.

listen.what: played fast like a bird (his nickname was Bird)

scales.tip: Black = press; o = octave key (left thumb).

scales.title: G major (written)
scales.tip: o = octave key. Upper D to G add the octave key to the lower fingering.

scales.title: D major, low octave
scales.tip: C♯ is all keys open; low D is all six.

songs.title: When the Saints Go Marching In

listen.name: Coleman Hawkins
listen.what: made the tenor a solo voice

remember: Top teeth rest on the mouthpiece. Your bottom lip is a soft cushion for the reed.
Left hand on top: B is finger 1, A is fingers 1-2, G is fingers 1-2-3.
Breathe in deep, then blow one steady, strong stream of air.
child.care: Wet the reed before you play. After, take the reed off and swab the water out.

beginner.build: Play long tones: hold one note steady while you count to 4.
beginner.play: Play songs with B, A and G, like “Hot Cross Buns.”
beginner.check: You can put the sax together and play B, A and G with a clear sound.

intermediate.build: Use the octave key to play high notes. Practice scales slowly.
intermediate.play: Breathe at the end of a musical sentence, not in the middle.
intermediate.check: You can play a song with low and high notes and an even sound.

advanced.build: Play all your scales, fast notes and fast tonguing. Try vibrato.
advanced.play: Make up your own solo in a jazz or blues song.
advanced.check: You can play a solo for people with a beautiful sound and good timing.

remember: Embouchure: top teeth on the mouthpiece, bottom lip over the teeth, mouth corners firm.
Left hand first: B (1), A (1-2), G (1-2-3), with the left thumb by the octave key.
Steady, supported air makes the tone. Don’t bite the reed.
teen.care: Rotate 3–4 reeds, swab the body and neck after every session, keep reeds in a reed case and keep the pads dry.

beginner.build: Long tones at a steady volume; start each note with the tongue (“too”).
beginner.play: Short melodies on G, A, B and C, breathing at the rests.
beginner.check: You can assemble the sax and play G, A, B and C with a steady tone and tongued starts.

intermediate.build: Octave key, chromatic notes and major scales (written C, G and F); long tones with a tuner.
intermediate.play: Band parts and melodies with planned breaths and dynamics.
intermediate.check: You can play two octaves in tune with an even tone and smooth slurs across the octave break.

advanced.build: All major scales, the chromatic scale across the full range, articulation styles and vibrato.
advanced.play: Improvise over a blues; play jazz and concert pieces in their own style.
advanced.check: You can perform a solo or jazz chart with consistent tone, steady time and your own improvised ideas.

remember: Single-reed embouchure: top teeth on the mouthpiece, lower lip cushioning the reed, firm corners, flat chin.
Keys shorten or lengthen the air column; the octave key opens a vent for the upper register.
A transposing instrument: alto sounds a major sixth below written (E♭), tenor a major ninth below (B♭).
adult.care: Rotate several reeds and store them flat in a case; swab after every session; dry the mouthpiece; have pads and corks checked yearly.

beginner.build: Long tones for steady tone and pitch; tonguing (tongue tip to reed tip); B, A, G and C fingerings.
beginner.play: Simple melodies with breaths planned at phrase ends.
beginner.check: You can assemble and care for the instrument and hold a steady, centered tone through one octave.

intermediate.build: Two-octave major scales and the chromatic scale; tuner work on long tones; slurs over the octave break.
intermediate.play: Ensemble parts with balanced dynamics and matched articulation.
intermediate.check: You can play the full standard range with even tone and pitch and match articulation in an ensemble.

advanced.build: All major and minor scales, arpeggios and patterns at tempo; varied articulation; controlled vibrato.
advanced.play: Improvisation over changes; stylistic interpretation of jazz and classical repertoire.
advanced.check: You can perform with your own tone and time, improvise coherently and adapt your sound to the style.

scales.title: Rock beat
scales.tip: Count out loud. Play where you see a mark.

scales.title: Rock beat
scales.tip: Hi-hat on every count; snare on 2 and 4.

scales.title: Kick on the “& of 3”
scales.tip: Same hands. Only the right foot changes.

scales.title: Sixteenth-note groove
scales.counts: 1 e & a 2 e & a 3 e & a 4 e & a
scales.tip: Hands alternate on the hat; snare still on 2 and 4.

scales.title: Half-time feel
scales.tip: Snare only on 3: the same tempo feels half as fast.

remember: Hold the sticks like a handshake, about a third of the way up.
Count out loud: 1, 2, 3, 4. The beat never stops.
Wear earplugs on a real drum kit.
child.care: Let the stick bounce up after each hit; that is kinder to the drums. Put your sticks away when you finish.

beginner.build: Let the stick bounce up after every hit: right, left, right, left, nice and even.
beginner.play: Play a rock beat: hi-hat on every count, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4.
beginner.check: You can keep a steady beat with a recording for a whole song.

intermediate.build: Learn rudiments like the paradiddle: R L R R, L R L L.
intermediate.play: Play a fill on the toms after 4 bars, then come back in right on time.
intermediate.check: You can play a beat with fills and never lose count.

advanced.build: Play rudiments fast and soft, not just fast and loud.
advanced.play: Play different styles like swing, funk and Latin beats.
advanced.check: You can play with a band, listen to everyone and keep the beat solid.

remember: Matched grip: the pivot point is between thumb and index finger, about a third up the stick.
Count 1-e-&-a out loud. Steady time comes before speed.
Protect your hearing: earplugs on any acoustic kit.
teen.care: Let sticks rebound (it saves drumheads and wrists), angle the cymbals, and keep sticks in a stick bag.

beginner.build: Single strokes at 60–80 BPM with a metronome, letting each stroke rebound.
beginner.play: The basic rock beat, then variations that move the kick drum.
beginner.check: You can hold a basic rock beat with a metronome for two minutes without speeding up.

intermediate.build: Essential rudiments (single and double stroke rolls, paradiddles, flams, drags) with accent patterns.
intermediate.play: Fills that land on beat 1 with a crash; shuffle and half-time feels; dynamics.
intermediate.check: You can play a whole song form (verse, chorus, fill, ending) from a chart, in time with other players.

advanced.build: Rudiments at every dynamic and tempo; ghost notes; heel-toe or double-pedal technique.
advanced.play: Swing, funk, Latin (bossa nova, songo) and odd meters; soloing over a vamp.
advanced.check: You can drive a band with solid time, choose the right groove for each style and solo musically.

remember: Matched grip with the fulcrum between thumb and index finger; let every stroke rebound.
Subdivide aloud (1-e-&-a). Steady time is the drummer’s first job.
Use hearing protection on acoustic drums; noise damage adds up and does not heal.
adult.care: Keep felts and sleeves on the cymbal stands, tune heads evenly lug by lug, and store sticks dry and straight.

beginner.build: Full strokes with rebound on a pad at 60–80 BPM; matching the sound of both hands.
beginner.play: A 4/4 rock beat with kick variations, counting aloud while playing.
beginner.check: You can hold a basic groove with a metronome at a steady tempo for the length of a whole song.

intermediate.build: Core rudiments (singles, doubles, paradiddles, flams, drags) with accents and dynamics.
intermediate.play: Fills that land on 1; shuffle, half-time and song form; balanced volume across the kit.
intermediate.check: You can follow a chart through a full song, play fills that support the form and lock in with the bass.

advanced.build: Rudimental vocabulary at every dynamic; ghost notes and linear patterns; brushes.
advanced.play: Authentic swing, funk, Latin and odd-meter grooves; solos built from motifs over a form.
advanced.check: You can lead an ensemble’s time, adapt instantly to style and dynamics and solo with structure.
